title: How To Keep Your Students Calm And Focused This Holiday Season ed-this-holiday-season/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin offers four strategies for keeping a classroom calm and productive during the excitable weeks before holiday break, when outside distractions like decorations, music, and anticipation tend to spill into the classroom. His recommendations are to slow down deliberately, since students take their emotional cues from the teacher's own pace and tone; to provide more frequent physical and mental breaks, including stretching or brief social time, so students can release restlessness and return focused; to increase the specificity and detail of instruction, since excitable students tend to produce sloppier work that requires more precise modeling; and to increase rather than lower expectations as break approaches, resisting the common tendency to ease standards during the holiday season. He frames the two weeks before a break as a predictable landmine that, with proactive adjustments to pace and expectations, can instead become a period of continued calm and even improvement.
points: Outside holiday distractions tend to spill into the classroom, increasing excitability, restlessness, and misbehavior in the weeks before break.
Students take emotional cues from the teacher's pace and tone, so deliberately slowing down helps counter outside excitement.
More frequent mental and physical breaks let students release restlessness productively before returning to focused work.
Excitable students tend to produce sloppier, less precise work, requiring teachers to increase rather than decrease instructional detail.
Teachers should resist the common tendency to lower expectations near a break, since easing standards signals that reduced attentiveness is acceptable.
quotes: Although your students may bring rambunctiousness and commotion with them from home, you control whether they keep it or surrender it out into the ether.
Mental and physical breaks become more essential the closer you get to vacation.
One of the negative byproducts of over-excited students is that their work becomes sloppy and less precise.
But this sends the message that it’s okay to be less attentive and have shoddy work habits, that a certain amount of misbehavior is expected.
You can subtly but powerfully alleviate the negative excitement and energy, the silliness and distraction, the impatience and impulsiveness.
